name: block-start regex stops excluding sub-headings
_note: RETARGETED 2026-09-01. It used to edit `ENTRY_ISH = re.compile(r'^\+##(?!#)')` in this same file; that literal no longer exists, because ENTRY_ISH is now DERIVED from BLOCK and BLOCK moved here from gen-dashboard.py. Left unrepaired the anchor would stop matching and the coverage would vanish silently — the third time in this repo that a refactor orphaned the mutation guarding it. ⚠ `expect` NAMES ONLY CASES IN THIS FILE'S OWN SUITE: `mutate_delivered` calls `run_suite(d, fname)` for the MUTATED FILE ALONE (check-plan-code.py:694), so a renderer case named here resolves to 0 red cases and the manifest fails. The first draft named `a level-3 heading does not split the entry` — a gen-dashboard case — and the Codex review half caught it by running `--mutate .`. The page-side blast radius of this same edit is covered by its own entry in gen-dashboard.json.
expect: the block-start rule excludes a sub-heading
a level-3 heading is not an entry attempt

name: the added-line rule is re-typed instead of derived
_note: NEW 2026-09-01, added by the Claude review half after the Codex half rated the agreement case Low ('verifies agreement, not derivation'). The point stands and this is the answer to it: the agreement case WAS load-bearing but nothing proved it fired, which by this repo's own standard is an unproven guard — the layer nothing checks back. Restoring a hand-written ENTRY_ISH is the exact regression the seam exists to prevent, and it is NOT covered by the BLOCK mutation: that one corrupts the shared rule so both sides move together and the agreement case stays green. Only breaking the DERIVATION separates them.

_note: backlog #84. CommonMark: a closer is at least as long as the opener. Dropping it lets a 3-backtick line close a 5-backtick block — exactly the shape anyone quoting markdown-inside-markdown writes, and the SKILL teaches people to quote it.
